headline: Connelly Early Baffles Mariners As Red Sox Keep Rolling In Seattle
morning_brew: Connelly Early was outstanding on the mound last night, keeping the Mariners completely off balance. He went six strong innings, giving up just one run on two hits and striking out seven. Wilyer Abreu broke things open with a massive two-run home run, and the bullpen shut the door with three scoreless frames. We took care of business with a five to one victory, and suddenly we have a little two-game win streak going out on the West Coast.

It is nice to see the young arms stepping up when we need them most. Early looked like a seasoned veteran out there, locating his pitches and keeping Seattle's hitters guessing all night. I haven't seen a rookie pitcher look this comfortable in a hostile environment since my buddy Sully tried to parallel park his Buick on a Friday night in the North End. The bats only got six hits, but they made them count, and that's the kind of situational hitting that has been missing for most of June.

Over in Foxborough, the chatter is all about the wide receiver room and whether the front office is going to carry seven guys on the roster. Troy Brown has been talking up the competition, and with young quarterback Drake Maye needing all the weapons he can get, this training camp battle is going to be fascinating. Back to baseball, the Sox have a chance to complete the sweep in Seattle this afternoon before heading to Colorado, so let's hope they keep the momentum rolling.

news_digest.headline: Will the Patriots keep seven wide receivers on their roster?
news_digest.dans_take: If we can find seven guys who can actually catch the ball, I say keep them all.
